To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the PTB is marked by a negative C-isotope excursion that is preceded by a series of transient excursions and is followed by a secondary peak of negative C-isotopes.

the Permian–Triasic boundary section at Guryur Ravine, Kashmir, India, exhibits a sequence of events that include a negative C-isotope excursion, secondary extinction peaks, and the main extinction horizon, and that these events are associated with a major eustacy and may record environmental disturbances prior to and during the end-Permian mass extinction.

the PTB section at Guryu Ravine, Kashmir, India, exhibits two transient negative δ13C excursions within the changxingensis Zone, which predate the LPEH by ∼ 400 kyr, that the LPEH is marked by the onset of a large negative δ13C shift, and that the Guryu Ravne section exhibits a step-wise extinction pattern with the largest peak at the LPEH.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following: 1) a detailed study of the Guryul Ravene section to provide a better understanding of the nature, cause(s), and timing of the PTB; 2) the development of a detailed chemostratigraphy for the Guryul section to provide a basis for comparison with other PTB sections; 3) a detailed comparison of the chemostratography of the Guryu and Meishan sections to determine whether these sections record similar

the following: (1) identification of a new negative C-isotopically anomalous horizon within the upper Changxing Formation that may be correlated to the negative C-isotope excursion observed within the Changhsing Formation in the Meisham section; and (2) identification of the LPEH in the Guryul Ravin section.
the nature of the PTB at a single section and the nature of the environmental changes associated with the PTB, and it is not concerned with the nature and timing of the PTB in general.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the PTB in the Guryul Ravene section is defined at the Zewan-Khunamuh contact, ∼ 260 cm below the biostratiographically defined PTB, based on a combination of biostratigraphy, chemostratigraphy, and sequence stratigraphy.

the LPEH is a major extinction event that is not associated with a bolide impact but may be associated with an intrinsic cause such as volcanism, which is supported by the evidence from Guryul Ravines.
the LPEH at Guryul is a major event that is marked by a negative C-isotope excursion that predates the PTB by ∼ 260 cm.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the LPEH at the Zewan Formation–Khunamush Formation contact is the best-defined PTB in the Guryul Ravne section.
the PTB is not a global event, but a local event, which is the reason why we can see a stepwise extinction in this area.

the Guryul Ravin section is a classic PTB section that is comparable to other classic sections such as the Meishan section, but it has the advantage of being much more complete, especially for the upper changxingensizone.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the LPEH is associated with a large negative carbon-isotopic excursion and a major eustatically induced sea level rise.

, in addition to providing a high-resolution, integrated record of the PTB interval, the Guryul Ravene section is a valuable archive that can be further explored to test the validity of different PTB correlation schemes and to better understand the environmental conditions and processes associated with the end-Permian mass extinction.
the LPEH is not a single event but rather a complex, multistage process that is expressed as a series of events in different locations and at different times.
